Mask of Truth. don't even have to think about it. I love the flavour text.

Edit: I mean, it might not qualify as tiny neccessarily, but it is my favourite tweak. If I had to give an alternative, the Megaton Hammer given it can effectively replace bombs.

I enjoy the little tweaks they made to the quality of life of the dungeons:

1. No loading between rooms 2. Enemies don't respawn every time you re-enter a room 3. More visual differentiation between rooms, and indicators of 'where to go next'

Taken together, I felt like I spent a lot less time backtracking back and forth between identical-looking rooms and re-killing the same annoying enemies, it made the dungeons I've always found the most annoying in the original (Jabu Jabu, Water Temple, Beneath the Well, Shadow Temple) a lot more tolerable (the free camera and motion-control aiming helps a lot in this regard as well).

Ganon is far more challenging in this plus i like their connecting totk ganondorf malice with the final boss but over all i like everything about the game.

So far for me (still relatively early in the game) it's the additions of scenes like the one Ollie mentioned - anyway, great to hear about all these tweaks and looking forward to seeing what others will mention in the comments, too!

I love that the camera is fully usable in castle town. Makes it far more alive and more tragic when it's all destroyed.

They could've easily kept it faithful, but chose to expand it greatly.

Lil’ Link is just so stinkin’ cute, runnin’ around bein’ all cute and stuff

Also being able to actually control the camera is a big win for me ☑️

There's a lot of changes that avoid blindly guessing or taking chances, and previous secrets are re-implemented so you aren't reliant on things like the Stone of Agony (that required the rumble pak sold separately).

There's much less "how was I supposed to know?" moments. On one hand it's more accessible, on the other hand it's less cryptic and mysterious when you stumble into something, or learn from another source. These were always the smaller things that you didn't need to do to beat the game, anyway.

My favorite tweak is how they made Link leaving the cutscene where he gets the Fairy Ocarina more impactful.

In the original, he takes a couple tentative steps back, then leaves using his normal running animation. You could interpret it as emotional, but it could’ve also been just him walking away since it’s the normal movement animation.

I like that they emphasized that small detail by making it more obviously emotional in the way Link leaves. Just a small detail that reinterprets the original material in a way that I thought they might have been going for, but was unclear due to hardware limitations.

@bluemujika 70? Someone didn't get to buy it from Walmart or Amazon for 60

Cutscenes in general are much improved while keeping the tone of the original. Link getting knocked TF out by Darunia had me in stitches. Ruto (especially in Japanese had the Ojousama mannerisms dialed up while somehow making her sound …less spoiled?), just Ruto. Anytime they lean on Zelda being a badarse is always a plus in my book and woo she’s even cooler y’all while still having an air of vulnerability and gravitas. They over did her guilt a bit though. Loved Impa as usual and Nabooru felt more like a warrior for justice this time around (she has never liked Ganondorf, but she really felt he didn’t deserve blind praise simply because he was their king due to a genetic quirk). They made Mido somewhat decent. I am anti bully and feel those types of people don't change, but I sorta felt bad for Mido.

I have never hated Navi, but I teared up when she left at the end. I really enjoyed hanging out with that little lightbulb. When you meet a great fairy her comment on the fountain made me laugh. You could almost hear her trying to figure out to become a great fairy. I do miss her hanging out in Link’s hat though.

I’ll admit muscle memory makes me not try a lot of stuff so I tend to notice scene changes, but I agree with bringing Epona to the gate. My eyebrows went up at that. Grottos are way easier to find (thank you!). I don’t like that redeads run at you now. F that. Somehow Dark Link feels like more of an ahole?

Morpha boss fight was fun this time. (As was Ganon). And the shadow and camera angle was good for my visually impaired self. I was concerned. I spend too much time reflecting back beamos lasers.

Also whomever designed new dead hand? Yeah I wanna cuss that person out.

My favorite though? THE ZORA ARE FREE (and all have the flu but still…)!!

How that stupid Owl doesnt ask if you understand, ITS THE BEST!!

Oh definitely the little tassels on Ganondorf's armour.

If I'm being serious, I liked that new item that allowed you to summon a business scrub at will. Didn't think I'd actually use them but they came in handy in a pinch.

The extra bits of context in the cutscenes are great. The story just makes more sense with them.

Just finished a 100% play through today and I have to say i'm mighty impressed.

I went back to play the original for the first time after beating the remake. Besides the obvious improvements like camera controls, being able to save and quit and be in the same area is game-changing. The first time I saved in the original was in Kakariko and when I opened the game to be back in Link's house, I was pretty peeved...

Also after dying to the big octorock and having to run back to the boss room every time with only 3 hearts, that was pretty annoying but I'm not sure if it works like that in the remake considering how few times I died. OoT64 is definitely harder, but i think it comes from the single stick control more than actual difficulty changes in the remake

Also one little note, I did see a lot of bad-faith haters complaining about the changed dialogue, but I have honestly enjoyed the original writing and lack of shoddy voice acting in the original more than the remake so far. It does kinda feel like they watered it down for the remake, and the voice acting does not help that at all... even if the cutscenes are pretty

@solarwolf07 Yeah, it's kind of funny how a lot of the difficulty change feels like it's mostly just due to the controls and camera being so much easier so you're not constantly getting merced by flaming bats you can't get the camera to focus on or whatever. It feels like you actually get fewer hearts and fairies and stuff in dungeons so I don't think it's like the game constantly giving you health that it didn't previously (aside from the fairy thoughts, if you get those).

The fact that you can wear masks as an adult! I actually specifically asked for this in a thread a couple weeks ago. Now I don't have to go back to child form every time I come across a new gossip stone just to find out what it says. And of course I can read everyone's thoughts in the future to find out how they have changed.

The emotional beats between link and saria are tweaked just enough, that my god. It just hits you like a bus. Even when you just talk to her at her spot outside the forest temple, that sense of leaving childhood is so intense in a way I did not expect

Probably thawing Zora's Domain. Nothing of substance to do there afterward which is why I'd consider it tiny but it was a big loose end to leave in the original and it's nice having the quick access tunnel from Lake Hylia working as an adult.

The movement, this is the best any character has controlled in possibly any game I've ever played. I was very worried that they were going to introduce momentum based movement like how characters control in more realistic AAA games (Uncharted for example seems to be the template for this and many other games in the same vain). But Link has a bit of that at the start of his run but they kept it very arcade like where any direction he goes is almost instant, combine that with being able to walk over any terrain and perform jumps and acrobatics in the environment and you're left with a result that enhances the greatest game of all time to an even higher level. The longer I played the game the more impressed I became with how intuitive it was to control Link and cannot praise the work the developers did enough.

For me it's Navi extra dialogue, sorry to disagree Gavin. But her having extra flavortext makes her feel more like a character than a tool to explain and target enemies. And now that she feels more like an individual the game feels like your playing it with a buddy! I even used her more not for actual help but because i was curious as to what she had to say.

I like that the Mask of Truth can actually be used to read minds now! It's not just backstory flavour, it functions like that for the player too.

@Ryu_Niiyama I really like how all the Zora caught a cold because they have been frozen 😄

@EarthboundBenjy Also just the fact that it can be worn as adult Link. You encounter and can speak to so many more of the gossip stones through just playing the game instead of having to back track as a child.

I like that the Gerudo's are a little more aggressive and mindful of their surroundings now. It made finding the carpenters more challenging!

The Cuccos thing is slightly harder as you now have to remember to jump. Along with loads of other bits being harder if your a dum dum and forget to jump. Some changes like the volley bit and the 2nd dungeon boss as child link are easier. And most of the time when you forget to jump and get punished your not even that annoyed about it and enjoy the challenge of remember to jump lol.

Haven't played a whole lot yet, but the lack of loading screens between buildings and most areas is pretty cool, and something I was hoping for. Being able to see into Lon Lon Ranch from Hyrule Field and then walk right in is pretty damn cool.

I like when you find Richard, the fat lady lets you ride her around Hyrule Town to say thanks

All replaying it has done for me is to wish there’s a new Zelda made in the same format. An “ocarina 2” if you like.

I love BotW and ToTK but damn this old setup is a joy to play. The old dungeons, creativity everywhere. It’s nice not having a stamina bar and a condensed world for a change. This to me really FEELS like a Zelda, much more than the new open world games do.

I'm only at Goron City (really taking my time to absorb everything) but so far, it's definitely the music. I don't know if that qualifies as a tiny tweak, but it truly makes the game even more special. I can't get enough.

There’s chanting in the music for the fire temple again. Albeit somewhat different than the original score

Poor Navi. She just can't catch a break, even if her interjections are just little speech bubbles now. Eternally cursed. lol

My number one favorite change is the orchestral score. It really goes hard, even when pushing/pulling the master sword. But yeah Nintendo knocked it out of the universe with this. WOW.

Lmao… for a moment I read “who’s your favorite tiny twink?” … and I was da fck?

Also… the most important one that couldn’t be done in the original. The Zora are free at last!

@ChromaticDracula The orchestral versions of the music are OUTSTANDING! I'm always curious how nobody seems to mention this...

My favourite minor tweak is that the hookshot can hit those eye switches now. That means you can legitimately 100% the water temple first if you want. Good change.

My least favourite tweak is how they've streamlined dungeons by taking out locks and keys. They don't feel as difficult or labyrinthian now.

@Aurumonado I always did water temple first ...Gotta rescue the wife before the friend!

@DanElectrode very true. On the topic of heart drops, I noticed that heart drops in the original seem to spawn three instead of one, which pleasantly surprised me haha

I’m not going to go into specifics and spoil anything, but for me it’s post-Water Temple Zora Domain.

I just love the ability to jump. Feels like some Mario game sometimes because I jump like an idiot everywhere 🤣 Especially from rock to rock, really funny to do !

I did not play much of the original, so I can't compare extensively, but one aspect I really like too is the fact you can explore cities at night now ! Kokiri forest is so beautiful at this time of day !

Putting Din's Fire in the Death Mountain GFF rather than the hidden Hyrule Castle one.

Breath of the wild references love.But a fairy now only heals 6 hearts not full health hate.

Difficult to remember because I only played Zelda Ocarina once back in the day, and revisiting it in recent years I was confronted with a blurring, clunky mess and barely lasted an hour in it. The remake is a godsend for someone like me eager to experience it again without suffering the many archaic elements that present themselves today.

I mostly notice that everything feels nicer. There's none of the clunkiness whether that be in the controls, obviously a vastly improved frame rate, and general design tweaks. One that I did note is the narrow path in the Fire Temple where a fall meant a long walk all the way back to trying it again. Boring! Now, Link will cling to the ledge and recover, or will fall into a lava pit, lose health, and respawn.

I bet this is one of the petty examples that IGN used to say this version of Ocarina is "easier" in its obvious agenda to not score it a 10. Whereas to sane people, the punishment from that fall is purely cheap game design. The path is easy to traverse as long as it's not rushed, so clinging to the ledge or losing health is an excellent two-stage warning to be careful compared to the previous brutal method after some simple carelessness. That is much more in sync with the ethos of Ocarina whereas in something like Ghosts N Goblins, that sort of cheap punishment is to be expected!

There are a lot of little things I like. Pro / Master HUD is great. Jumping changes gameplay. The cutscenes are astonishing, especially the scene you get the master sword for the first time. The environment changes with the modern rendering makes everything feel more natural and true to their vision. And as others mentioned, the orchestral music is just beautiful.

All great but the best? It’s the three C’s. Character, Camera, and Controls for me.

We take it for granted but dual sticks and 100% camera control makes such a fundamental difference in the gameplay that I truly believe it will surprise many how it feels to go back to play the original. It just gives me even more freedom. Ocarina of Time was the first game I played on N64. It was my first 3D game and introduced me to “open worlds”. To now experience that with modern camera controls with all the other changes just really seals the deal for me. Link does what I want, when I want it, and how I want. I never feel cheated. I feel like when I run up and jump near Epona, it just works and Link mounts correctly. I like when I walk around with my shield up, he keeps walking forward but I can pivot my shield to the left or right. I can control my sword swing direction. I can swing the camera just where I need it and it doesn’t clip into the environment. They way Link responds to all my inputs just feels… right.

A lot of people will go back to the original. It was will still hold up very well, but all things considered, the camera controls makes the biggest difference to me. I can say so far, this is my favourite version of Ocarina of Time and I am surprised I feel this way. This game beat my expectations.

If I had any minor criticisms about the controls, it’s simply the fact I can’t be as hardcore as in the N64 version, and I don’t have a separate dedicated button to raise my shield while Z-targeting like in the original version.

They nailed the feeling of walking on ice! The frosting and the snow in the Ice Cavern is amazing. Actually made me reach for a blanket!

#4153. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4152. Marathon’s Symbiosis Update Adds Host Of New Modes, Including Permanent PvE, Next Month

Bungie has detailed its upcoming Symbiosis update for Marathon, which introduces several significant modes next month. Chief among them is the new permanent PvE mode, which Bungie previously experimented with and promised earlier this year.

Symbiosis is headlined by Expedition, a co-op PvE destination with roguelite elements. Expedition pits teams of players against escalating challenges and offers randomized upgrades called Flash Boosts to increase their odds of success.

The Perimeter zone has also been expanded with the new Burrows and Reservoir areas. Another addition is Limbo, a new social hub for players to gather that features a firing range. You can also try out the new sword-wielding Bishop Runner Shell alongside new weapons and gear, such as the Maverick pistol, throwing knife, hack grenade, and V17 flamethrower. Lastly, you can test your skills against other players in the beta PvP Deathmatch mode.

Symbiosis arrives in Marathon on December 8. An open play week will kick off the same day, allowing new players to experience all of Marathon’s content for free until December 15.

The Symbiosis update marks Marathon's evolution into a more co-op-friendly, PvE experience as its initial focus on PvP extraction has struggled to sustain a substantial audience since its March 5 launch. Bungie announced in September that it plans to spend the rest of 2026 improving Marathon's core mechanics and features while giving players more agency for how they engage with it beyond competitive PvP.

For more on Marathon, check out our review.

#4151. Here's Everything We Saw During The MagicCon Atlanta Preview Panel

We've got all the big news from the MagicCon Atlanta Preview Panel, which focuses on in-universe updates for 2027.

The Magic: The Gathering preview panel from MagicCon Atlanta brought us a much-needed deeper look at Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, the first Magic set on the 2027 release calendar, and also confirmation of a Netflix animated show.

In this blog, we'll summarize all the big announcements from the panel, hosted by British radio and TV host (and, most importantly, Magic fan) Jack Saunders, joined by head of story Roy Graham, head designer (and vision designer for Nauctis) Mark Rosewater, and Nauctis world building lead Laurel Pratt.

The stream kicked off with the reveal that the Magic: The Gathering community has raised $10 million for Extra Life through the ongoing philanthropic efforts, including Secret Lair drops, specific Extra Life products, and straight-up donations.

It was also revealed that 100% of the money from purchases of Extra Life products at MagicCon Atlanta will be donated to Extra Life; for products purchased in any other way, the split is a smaller percentage. So, if you're at the show and want to pick up some of the collection, your money goes further with a direct purchase!

Mark Rosewater kicks this off by hyping up the move to an underwater plane and says this has been in the works for 20 years. There were a lot of challenges, including how to represent the flying mechanic! The answer... there's no flying!

Then it was confirmed that a new mechanic is coming, called Dive, and it won't be as straightforward as a creature feature.

Laurel Pratt then takes us through how building a set underwater works, and how the team has to use research to represent the color pie. Roy Graham then takes over to talk about The Shallows, the first area within Nauctis. Dungeons & Dragons gets a callout for being the inspiration for this set, for how the tabletop game handles similar situations.

We finally get our first card for Nauctis: Calmwater Mentor, a Seal Monk! It's a four-mana mono-white card, and when it enters, you search your library for up to two creature cards with power 2 or less, reveal them, put them in your hand, then shuffle your library. We also get a look at the card in the Coral Frame, which is available in boosters and collector boosters.

The next card is Goramou the Coral Taken, a green-red Shark that confirms Blood tokens are coming back as a big mechanic.

Next, we're heading to a new area: The Grand Marine, home of the Merfolk and Hominids. We get some talk about the importance of Merfolk and their history in Magic, and how the team plans to fairly represent the creature type in this set. We then get a look at Shimmering Citadel, a white-blue dual land that enters tapped. It also has the Exhaust ability, returning from Aetherdrift, which costs five mana to let you draw two cards and gain one life, but you put a depletion counter on the land.

We go straight into another card, Salinae, the Ocean Mother, an eight-mana mono-blue Whale God with devotion to blue, but it's pointed out that this is the only card with it in the set. Five Whale Gods will feature in the set and be hugely important to the colors they are associated with.

Box Toppers are confirmed as returning for all booster types, and they will be known as Sunken Treasures.

We move on to The Abyss next, and start exploring the hulking, terrifying creatures that occupy this corner of Nauctis. The first card we see here is Tecton, Malignant Ruin, which sees the return of Descent. This 5/5 costs one mana less to cast for each card in your graveyard, has Menace and Deathtouch, and whenever you sacrifice a card, you draw a card. This is an example of a Desolator, the creature type revealed in the MagicCon Detroit ticketed play events.

Abyssal Lotus has been revealed: a zero-cost artifact that you can tap and exile for three mana of any color if you Descend 8. It is the headline card of the set and comes in three variants: regular, Coral Frame, and Raised Foil Headliner.

Following the Reality Fracture panel at MagicCon Amsterdam, we know exactly what 2027 looks like for MTG, including all sets and big events.

That's everything we're getting for Nauctis! Roy Graham stays behind with Jack Saunders, and they're going to talk about publishing updates for Magic. There's a recap of Omens of Chaos, and confirmation that more novels are coming, tied into in-universe sets!

We then get the recap of Untold Stories, a comic series in partnership with Dark Horse, that focused on Jace, Elspeth, and Liliana, but Roy confirms that Chandra is up next!

Mage of Zhalfir is then hyped, with a few pages shown from the first issue, along with some backstory for the narrative.

Kamigawa: Titanbreach then has its Moon Over the Neon City novel confirmed, and it will get a Command Tower promo card with it! Author Akemi Dawn Bowman returns, having previously worked on Kamigawa: Neon Dynasties. It's coming on July 27, 2027.

Then comes a surprising reveal: The Incoming Student's Guide to Strixhaven, an in-world visual history of the hugely popular plane.

Two more books are then revealed: a Planeswalker Encyclopedia and a Magic: The Gathering Bestiary, both coming in September 2027.

While only in early development, Magic: The Gathering is finally getting an animated Netflix series. The show is called Planeswalkers, and it's coming in 2027!

The story team at Wizards has been involved with the production of the series since day one, and based on the early sneak peeks we just saw, it's looking incredible.

Our favorite Boggarts are here to show everything that they've been getting up to on their podcast over the past year. This includes a sizzle reel of the videos they've been featured in since Lorwyn Eclipsed was released.

It's a bit of a comedy break, with nothing notable actually being revealed during this section of the show.

Jack Saunders then comes back and introduces Brian Henson of The Jim Henson Company, who talks about how Squen & Cragg came to life and the experience of working with Magic: The Gathering as a brand.

We then get a detailed look at how Squen & Cragg work, plus an amazing look at the puppeteers involved.

Squen & Cragg are then revealed to have stickers and pets that have shadowdropped in MTG Arena

The show just kinda ends from there; it was a weird and slightly disappointing end to a preview panel that should have been about in-universe sets for next year, but didn't really go any further than Nauctis. We also don't feel like we got the monumental announcements promised in the lead-up, as cool as the Netflix show is.

A good show, but not what it was hyped up to be at all.

#4149. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4148. Surprising Literally Nobody, Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Most Pre-Ordered Game In PlayStation And Xbox Store History

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19. You can preload the game on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S starting today, as detailed by Rockstar Games, PlayStation, and Xbox. Alongside this announcement, both PlayStation and Xbox have revealed that – surprise! – GTA VI is the most preordered game in the history of their respective digital stores.

That's not shocking – GTA VI is, by many metrics, the most anticipated game in history, with its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, selling nearly 235 million copies since its launch back in 2013. There's also the fact that Rockstar Games is not releasing a physical edition of GTA VI, per se. Yes, you can go to a store to pick up a GTA VI box (and you can do so today, allowing you to preload the game), but inside that box will be a download code for a digital version of the game – you won't find GTA VI on a physical disc. So, naturally, many players are opting to purchase the game on digital storefronts like the PlayStation and Xbox game stores.

"Grand Theft Auto VI, the most preordered title of all time on the Microsoft Store, launches November 19," an Xbox blog post reads. "Considering the unprecedented demand, we encourage everyone to begin preloading as soon as possible to ensure you're prepared for launch day." PlayStation echoes this statement with a blog post of its own that reads, "Grand Theft Auto VI is now the most preordered game in the history of the PlayStation Store. Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start preloading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day."

There you have it: People are very excited about Grand Theft Auto VI.

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about its tropical storms and hurricanes. Be sure to read about how GTA VI will target 30 FPS gameplay on all consoles, too.

#4147. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.
